headline: A lake pilgrimage and a quiet car ride to beach: last hours of sisters who took own lives in Brighton

members.title: Three sisters who drowned in Brighton decided to end their own lives, inquest finds
members.lead: Coroner records finding of suicide in deaths of Jane Adetoro, Christina Walters and Rebecca Walters from London in May Three sisters who drowned in the sea in Brighton collectively decided to end their own lives, a coroner has ruled. The bodies of Jane Adetoro, 36, Christina Walters, 32, and Rebecca Walters, 31, all from London, were recovered from the sea off Brighton in the early hours of 13 May. In the UK and Ireland, Samaritans can be contacted on freephone 116 123. In the US, you can call or text the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline at 988 or chat at 988lifeline.org. In Australia, the crisis support service Lifeline is 13 11 14. Other international helplines can be found at befrienders.org Continue reading...

members.title: A lake pilgrimage and a quiet car ride to beach: last hours of sisters who took own lives in Brighton
members.lead: Inquest hears details of how three women spent their final days but why they ended their lives may never be known Jane Adetoro and her younger sisters Christina and Rebecca Walters were “the closest sisters and the best friends”, according to their family. Devoted to their father, Joseph, whom they messaged every day, the adult siblings lived quiet lives in the flat they shared in west London and would do everything together. When they died in May this year, it was no different. Early in the morning of 13 May, the sisters’ bodies were recovered from the sea in Brighton, hours after a taxi had dropped the three women at the beachfront. Continue reading...
